Continuing education for Texas counselors

Ethics CEUs

Texas LPCs need 24 hours of continuing education each renewal period, at least 6 of them in ethics. Reem Glasco, LPC-S, offers ethics continuing education in two formats: one CEU online, or two CEUs in person, held on a trail walk among horses near Dripping Springs. The subject is secondary trauma: what this work does to the people who do it, and where the ethical obligations actually sit.

Email about the next session The CE requirements in full

The two formats

Both count as ethics hours. The in-person session is the one that is hard to find anywhere else.

Why secondary trauma, for an ethics hour

Ethics continuing education is often taught as a tour of the rules: boundaries, record keeping, dual relationships, the things you already know and will be reminded of once every two years. That version is survivable and forgettable.

Secondary trauma gets at the part of ethics that actually goes wrong in practice. Competence is an ethical obligation, and competence degrades when a clinician is depleted in ways they have stopped noticing. Most ethical failures in this field are not decisions made badly; they are attention that was no longer there.

So the session looks at what accumulates across a caseload, how it shows up before you can name it, what the obligation to monitor your own fitness to practice means concretely, and when it requires you to do something about it.

Walking it, rather than sitting through it

The two-CEU version is held outdoors, walking, among horses. That is not a gimmick attached to the content; it is the content. A room full of therapists discussing depletion while sitting still for two hours is its own small joke. Walking changes what people say, and horses respond to the state of the person in front of them rather than the credential.

It also means you leave having practiced the thing rather than having heard about it.

Who it is for

  • Texas LPCs filling the 6 required ethics hours per renewal period
  • LPC Associates, who need the same hours
  • Clinicians who suspect they are running on empty and would rather find out on purpose

Questions about the CEUs

How many ethics CEUs do Texas LPCs need?

At least 6 hours of ethics within the 24 hours of continuing education required each renewal period. Passing the jurisprudence exam counts as one of those ethics hours. LPC Supervisors need a further 6 hours of supervision-specific CE, counted inside the same 24.

Do these hours count toward the approved-provider half?

Since 1 January 2024 at least half of your 24 hours must come from a provider listed in 22 TAC §681.140(f). Confirm the provider status of any CE before you book it, including this one, because hours from an unlisted provider are still worth taking but do not fill that half.

What does the trail walk session involve physically?

Walking at conversation pace on a trail, with time standing among horses. It is not strenuous and there is no riding, but it is outdoors in central Texas, so it is weather dependent and gets rescheduled rather than pushed through.

Can LPC Associates attend?

Yes. Associates carry the same continuing education requirements as fully licensed LPCs and are welcome at both formats. Associates supervised by Reem are included in the annual retreat as part of their supervision.

How do I register?

Email reemglasco@gmail.com and ask about the next session. Dates and fees are not yet published here, so email is currently the only route.
